question: Where does annealing sit, and what is the DS product form: single strands purified then annealed, or duplex handled throughout; duplex powder or two strand powders?
why_it_matters: Drives UF membrane MWCO, the filtration analysis, and the spray-dry decision.
notes: Evidence (SRC-ALMAC-2023, SRC-HONGENE, SRC-CODEXIS): dsRNA nick-sealing ligases require a duplex nick, so annealing is INTERLEAVED with ligation and the product is co-assembled as a duplex (~14-17 kDa). This creates TENSION with the brief's ~7 kDa (single-strand) UF basis. Confirm intended base case.

question: What is the real annual DS demand (kg/yr)?
why_it_matters: Governing sizing input; all capacity, duty, and campaign numbers are functions of it.
notes: Scenarios S1-S3 are illustrative placeholders only (scenarios.csv).

question: Ligation conversion achievable for our fully modified 21-mer at kg scale?
why_it_matters: Sets yield and drives whether partial-product removal load is manageable.
notes: CLOSED for PER-LIGATION conversion, with a caveat: >92% single-feed / >94% split-feed on fully modified siRNA blocks in continuous flow, held >100 h (SRC-CN119265174). Overall CAMPAIGN mass yield is a different quantity, 19-43% (SRC-HONGENE-BROCHURE-2025). Our own kg-scale conversion is still open. See P-LIG-CONV, P-YIELD-OVERALL-PUB.

question: Block full-length purity achievable for our short modified blocks?
why_it_matters: Sets the internal-limited purity floor (Pi f_i) that filtration cannot fix.
notes: NARROWED, not closed, and the band in this note CORRECTED 2026-09-25. It previously quoted 89-96 percent as the measured chromatography-free purity. That band is retracted: its low end was an 89.1 percent purity measured at 6.00 g, a BENCH datum presented inside a range labelled 145-258 g, a 25-40x scale misattribution. The chromatography-free hectogram measurements are 93.6, 94.8 and 95.6 percent (SRC-WO2020227618), and the point value formerly carried as 92 was a YIELD, not a purity - the source reads 'deoxy-TTACC 5mer (145.5 g, 57.8 mmol, 92.4% yield, 93.6% purity)'. The nearest-chemistry datum is 81 percent for a 6-mer 2'-OMe PS (SRC-KELLY-OPRD-2025), which is OUR backbone but the wrong topology and 12.6 points below the band; it is deliberately NOT merged in, because merging two chemistries into one range would manufacture a band neither of them supports - the consequence of that exclusion is published as a sensitivity on the ligation envelope page instead. Nobody has published the number for short 2'-OMe/2'-F/PS blocks carrying a 5'-phosphate. See P-BLOCK-PUR, ENV-001, ENV-002, Q-057.

question: Step yields (ligation, UF/DF, evaporation, drying) for our system?
why_it_matters: Mass balance inputs; currently assumptions.
notes: BOUNDED, not closed. Dryer 61-89% optimised (8.6-22% unoptimised, SRC-KAPIL-2025); UF/DF loss is an equation not a constant (SRC-MILLIPORE-TFF, SRC-NOURAFKAN-2024, see EQ-UFYIELD); overall ligation-route campaign yield 19-43% (SRC-HONGENE-BROCHURE-2025). Evaporation yield remains wholly unsupported (P-YLD-EVAP). See P-YLD-*.

question: Ligation reactor product concentration (g/L) achievable?
why_it_matters: Sets reactor batch volume and downstream volumes.
notes: RESTATED 2026-09-25, and the restatement REOPENS it rather than narrowing it. This note previously read that the question was closed at the demonstrated level of 1 mM, about 14-16 g/L. That presented as a settled titre the same number P-CONC-LIG now carries as an upper BOUND: the sentence it comes from states the concentration at which synthesis was ACHIEVED, and the paper reports no conversion, yield or purity anywhere - verified by counting, the whole text contains exactly one percent sign, in '100% v/v methanol'. So there is a CEILING and no floor, and anyone sizing U01-LIG from this row as it previously stood would have undersized the vessel and with it the buffer suite, the membrane area and the CIP loop. WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS A LOWER BOUND: one conversion, yield or purity figure beside the 1 mM charge would supply it. The segment-side evidence does not help, because its two ends are a success and a failure and are not a range at any width (P-LIG-SEG-CONC, ENV-006, Q-064) - and as of 2026-09-27 the void's WIDTH is unknown too, between about 2x and about 6x, because the low end is quoted per segment plus a supported template hub and the high end states no basis at all. This note said 6.7x flatly until then. The coupling makes this worse than a bookkeeping gap: a lower titre means a larger vessel, and a larger vessel is exactly where the 65 C anneal ramp fails on jacket area (CPL-006, Q-065), so an unbounded volume also leaves that equipment fork undecidable. See P-CONC-LIG, Q-034.

question: Maximum UF concentration before viscosity/osmotic limit?
why_it_matters: Decides whether evaporation is needed at all, and its duty.
notes: CLOSED at bench scale: ~193 g/L for siRNA on a charged 10 kDa membrane (SRC-ZYDNEY-2025); 200 mg/mL at >=95% yield and <15 cP for a single-strand antisense oligo on 3 kDa (SRC-GRONKE-2023). Viscosity is NOT what stops it. Our stream's ceiling and its cause (osmotic vs fouling) are open - see Q-041. See P-CONC-UF.

question: Evaporator outlet concentration / viscosity limit for this stream?
why_it_matters: Sets evaporation duty and dryer feed solids.
notes: CLOSED in kind: thin-film evaporation of an oligonucleotide drug substance is established practice, with 160 mg ASO/g solution achieved in manufacture (SRC-PMC7415879) - a single-strand ASO, not our duplex. TRAP: that paper's 'few hours' is a batch cycle time, not a residence time. Our stream's U, viscosity limit and foaming remain gaps. See P-CONC-EVAP.

question: Spray-dryer feed solids target?
why_it_matters: Sets dryer water load and energy duty.
notes: See P-CONC-DRYFEED.

question: Diafiltration diavolumes for our buffer exchange and final matrix swap?
why_it_matters: Dominant WFI and aqueous-waste driver.
notes: CLOSED for the theory, open for our stream. Vendor diavolume tables reproduce the site's removal percentages exactly (SRC-PALL-TFF; 5 DV=99.3%, 7 DV=99.9%); a nucleic-acid process is documented at 4-6 diavolumes (SRC-HUSSON-CIRCRNA-2025). See P-DF-DIAVOL, EQ-DIAF.

question: Excipient:API ratio and final spray-dry matrix composition?
why_it_matters: Sets powder mass, dryer load and duplex protection. Reframed: the excipient is for the DRYER, not the molecule.
notes: CLOSED in one direction. Four of seven approved siRNA products carry NO weighed excipient at all, at 160-200 mg/mL in essentially pure water (SRC-SIRNA-LABELS), so the active needs no stabilising excipient in the liquid state. Any excipient in a dried matrix is a drying/powder aid. No dried siRNA product has ever been approved, so no ratio transfers. The question is now what ratio the DRYER needs. See P-EXCIPIENT-RATIO, BUF-FINAL.

question: What is the glass transition of the dried product at its achieved residual moisture, and what storage temperature does that imply?
why_it_matters: Sets the post-drying thermal margin, which is far tighter than an anhydrous-trehalose figure suggests - and binds BEFORE the melting temperature (higher priority than Q-030).
notes: CLOSED for the constants: Gordon-Taylor k=4.76 for trehalose (SRC-GELMAN-2016); anhydrous trehalose is 389 K or 380 K depending on the primary; anhydrous sucrose 343 K. Spray-dried trehalose siRNA measured Tg 38-53 C at 3.8-4.6% residual moisture (SRC-KEIL-2021), well below the melting temperature (Q-030). Drives storage and handling, not just dryer outlet. See EQ-TG, R-003.

question: Modified-siRNA duplex melting temperature (Tm)?
why_it_matters: Spray-dryer outlet must stay below Tm, but Tg (Q-039) binds first - Tm is the looser of the two limits.
notes: Bound, not closed for our sequence: 58.1 C unmodified 21-mer; 60.4-64.1 C with 2'-F or 2'-OMe at three positions, in 100 mM NaCl (SRC-MALEK-2019). DO NOT extrapolate the +1 to +2 C/nt increment across all 21 positions - it was measured over three. Tm (58-64 C) sits ABOVE the moisture-shifted powder Tg of 38-53 C, so the glass transition binds first (Q-039). See R-003.

question: Does chemical modification make aggressive nuclease control unnecessary?
why_it_matters: Sizes the contamination-control strategy for the aqueous train.
notes: HALF closed. Modification is protective by ~1000-fold in plasma half-life and protection is POSITIONAL - internal 2'-modification protects, terminal caps do not (SRC-LAYZER-2004, SRC-CZAUDERNA-2003). This is SERUM challenge, not a manufacturing hold. Nobody has measured nuclease from process bioburden in a hold vessel for any modality; that half stays open, search recorded as failed.

question: Quantitative enzyme (ligase) clearance, for whichever enzyme form is chosen (soluble or immobilised)?
why_it_matters: Linchpin for a chromatography-free train; currently unproven at scale.
notes: RESTATED TWICE. (1) From 'not yet found' to NOT PUBLICLY AVAILABLE: no ppm, log-reduction, immunoassay or total-protein figure for ligase clearance exists in any patent, paper or vendor document the dive read, and it read the whole relevant patent estate (SRC-CODEXIS-PATENTS, SRC-NEB-WO2023173098, SRC-CN119265174, SRC-T7RNAP-2024). The one adjacent number is inverted in size ratio and does not transfer. (2) 2026-09-21, MADE FORM-AGNOSTIC: the question previously read '...with immobilised enzyme', which presupposed the answer to Q-050. Enzyme form is undecided, so clearance is carried as TWO branches, neither asserted as chosen - denature then depth filtration for a soluble enzyme, retention on the carrier for an immobilised one. The soluble branch is not free: an 85 C denature hold sits above any plausible duplex Tm (R-021, Q-030). Linchpin for a chromatography-free train; R-002, R-021. See P-ENZ-CLEARANCE-LRV and Q-050.

question: What capability does the route demonstrate on drug-substance purity, and can the toxicology programme qualify what it leaves behind?
why_it_matters: The DS purity criterion is not a fixed public number; it is derived from the applicant's own batch capability, so the route's demonstrated capability is what matters.
notes: RESTATED (F-014, F-022). There is no published full-length percentage or single-impurity limit for any approved siRNA DS in five jurisdictions (SRC-PMDA-ONPATTRO and siblings); the criterion is set from the applicant's own toxicology batches and tightened as batches accumulate (SRC-FDA-OXLUMO-CHEMR, SRC-FDA-INCLISIRAN-CHEMR, SRC-PATISIRAN-EPAR). A structurally capped route sets its spec at its own capability and must qualify above-threshold impurities toxicologically rather than purify them away. Oligonucleotides are outside ICH Q3A/Q6A scope (SRC-ICH-Q3A-SCOPE).

question: What product titre (g/L) does the enzymatic ligation route actually reach?
why_it_matters: Sets reactor batch volume alongside P-CONC-LIG; a vendor titre previously quoted here had no source.
notes: CLOSED at the demonstrated level: ~1 mM (~14-16 g/L) exemplified (SRC-ALMAC-2023, SRC-WO2025262452); '100 g/L' is unsupported. A '30 g/L titer' once attributed to the vendor blog does not appear there. See P-CONC-LIG, Q-016.

question: Which membrane molecular-weight cut-offs were tested for siRNA ultrafiltration, and what is the upper limit for adequate duplex retention?
why_it_matters: Decides UF membrane selection for a ~7 kDa strand or ~17 kDa duplex.
notes: REFUTED on the old figure, still open on the enumeration. The '1/3/10/30 kDa, 30 kDa upper limit' is unsupported and must not be repeated. What is quotable points the OTHER way: an oligonucleotide should be at least twice the MWCO for robust retention (SRC-GRONKE-2023), the 3-6x-lower vendor rule (SRC-SCHWARTZ-BPI-2003, SRC-PALL-TFF), and 10 kDa in the only siRNA optimisation study (SRC-ZYDNEY-2025). The Zydney siRNA study's own cut-off list is still unavailable, so this stays open on that point. See SRC-ZYDNEY-2024.

question: What permeate flux and product recovery does an oligonucleotide UF/DF step actually achieve?
why_it_matters: Membrane area sizing and yield; currently carried on protein and plasmid-DNA surrogates from a weak secondary source.
notes: PARTIALLY closed. 40-100 mg/mL routine for oligonucleotide UF/DF (SRC-PMC7415879); sieving <0.008 achievable (SRC-GRONKE-2023). Hold-up (30-40% for mRNA at small scale, SRC-NOURAFKAN-2024) dominates loss at small batch. No siRNA-specific flux number exists in anything reachable. See P-UFDF-RETENTION, P-UFDF-HOLDUP-LOSS, R-011.

question: What are the real bioburden and endotoxin limits for an oligonucleotide drug substance process?
why_it_matters: Sizes the contamination-control strategy and hold-time policy for the whole aqueous train.
notes: BIOBURDEN closed, ENDOTOXIN still open. <1 CFU/mL demonstrates microbial control at DS, a statement of practice with a case-by-case escape, not a limit (SRC-PMC7415879); the compendial floor (TAMC 2000/TYMC 200 per g or mL) is three orders looser (SRC-PHEUR-5-1-4). There is NO compendial endotoxin ladder: the limit is calculated from dose (per mg of substance), so the old per-mL ladder was the wrong kind of quantity and has been removed. R-012 is closed by this.

question: Where is the spray-drying excipient introduced: at the final diafiltration, or after evaporation?
why_it_matters: Decides the evaporator duty and the viscosity limit, and therefore whether evaporation has meaningful work to do at all.
notes: Risk R-005 requires salts to be exchanged OUT at the final DF but does not require the excipient load IN at that point. Adding it after evaporation keeps evaporator duty and viscosity down. Base case here is post-evaporation. See P-EXCIP-FRAC-PRE-EVAP, Q-021.

question: How is the ATP requirement reconciled with the ATP ceiling that suppresses the adenylylated dead end?
why_it_matters: The ATP a multi-junction assembly consumes and the ATP that suppresses the adenylylated dead end pull in opposite directions, and R-010 cannot fix the dead end downstream because it differs from the product by about 329 Da. The charge also draws down free magnesium, which propagates into the diafiltration load through the one species the register says does not diafilter.
notes: REWRITTEN 2026-09-25 - the tension is real, the framing was not. This note previously set 'at least 4 mM ATP' against 'less than 100 uM' as though the feasible window were empty. Both quotes are verbatim, but the first is THE STATEMENT OF THE PROBLEM ITS DOCUMENT'S INVENTION SOLVES, not an operating condition: SRC-WO2025262452 teaches 'less than about 4 mM ATP ... optionally ... 0.5 mM or less' in four places, says its regeneration system 'overcomes the requirement for high concentrations of ATP', and claims complete ligation with 'sub-stoichiometric quantities of ATP or AMP'. The suppression side is softer too - SRC-PBCV1-2014 reports little inhibition at 1 mM ATP for most sequences. So no empty window is claimed anywhere, and the earlier inference that fed-batch has no demonstration is also withdrawn: in-situ generation from AMP and polyphosphate is the mechanistic equivalent of ATP-limited feeding and IS exemplified, subject to its own ceiling of 'a maximum of 66 % conversion to ATP'. WHAT REMAINS OPEN is the setpoint for OUR enzyme and the second coupling, which nobody had registered: ATP chelates magnesium about one for one, so the charge draws down the free cation the ligase needs and raising total magnesium to compensate loads the species that resists diafiltration (CPL-001, CPL-002, R-014, IMP-DIVALENT). See C-003, P-LIG-ATP, BUF-LIG.

question: What actually sets the ultrafiltration ceiling for our stream - osmotic pressure or fouling?
why_it_matters: Viscosity is not the limiter (Q-017); knowing which mechanism binds decides membrane and operating choices.
notes: If viscosity is only ~120 mPa.s at 500 mg/mL (SRC-PMC7415879, secondary report), viscosity is not what stops ultrafiltration. Whether osmotic pressure or fouling sets the ceiling for our stream is unresolved. See Q-017, P-CONC-UF.

question: Which instrument measures retentate concentration at the UF/DF endpoint, given that fixed-pathlength in-line UV saturates on a 21-mer at process concentration?
why_it_matters: An in-line UV concentration reading is standard PAT. On a 21-mer at process concentration the pathlength an A260 = 1 reading needs is a few microns, so a conventional fixed cell (2-10 mm) saturates by three orders of magnitude. What replaces it decides whether the UF/DF endpoint is a closed control loop or an open one judged on a withdrawn sample.
notes: PARTIALLY RESOLVED, AND ONE EARLIER READING OF IT WAS WRONG. What holds: fixed-pathlength in-line UV saturates - INFERENCE (ours), arithmetic in gen/controls.py from P-EPS-260 and the stream concentration. What was WRONG: this row previously said the deployed answer 'is variable-pathlength slope spectroscopy, which is at-line, not in-line'. That is a property of the BENCHTOP SoloVPE, not of the technique. FlowVPE publishes 5 um to 8 mm and is used IN-LINE on UF/DF in the peer-reviewed literature (SRC-ROLINGER-2023, open access; corroborated by SRC-BHANGALE-2022), and FlowVPX catalogues a 260 nm GMP light source with 21 CFR part 11, IQ/OQ and CSV (SRC-REPLIGEN-FLOWVPX). The TRUE constraint is narrower and quantitative: at P-CONC-UF the required pathlength falls below the published in-line floor P-VPE-PATHLENGTH-MIN, so on THIS stream the reading comes off a withdrawn sample. That is why control C-013 is control_type at_line_only rather than not_measurable. Residual gaps in Q-051; the extinction coefficient in Q-052.

question: What are the hold-time limits on the aqueous intermediates?
why_it_matters: The whole train is aqueous with a growth-promoting ligation buffer; hold times drive the contamination-control strategy and the microbial specifications.
notes: No published hold-time study exists for any oligonucleotide process. EU GMP and EMA guidance set a 24 h default beyond which holds must be justified with data, and supply none (SRC-EMA-STERILISATION-2019, SRC-STANDARDS-CURRENT). A hold-time protocol is a named technology-transfer gap (SRC-WHO-TRS1044). See R-009.

question: In which analytical dimension will the drug-substance purity specification be written?
why_it_matters: Purity multiplies only within one analytical dimension, so the dimension chosen decides which purity the block-ligation floor must clear.
notes: Duplex purity by non-denaturing chromatography is NOT the product of two denaturing single-strand purities and can read higher than either (SRC-FDA-OXLUMO-CHEMR; the EMA draft requires impurity specs on each single strand AND on the duplex, SRC-EMA-OLIGO-2024). EQ-PURITY multiplies block full-length fractions, which is sound within one dimension only. See Q-011, Q-033.

question: What are the evaporator thermal operating point (feed and vacuum boiling temperatures) and the plant heat-loss fraction?
why_it_matters: Set the evaporator sensible-heat and loss duties in the full energy balance; latent heat alone is only the minimum and understates the real load.
notes: Feeds P-EVAP-T-FEED, P-EVAP-T-BOIL and P-HEAT-LOSS-FRAC. The vacuum operating point is chosen to hold the duplex well below its Tm; boiling-point elevation rises as solutes concentrate (EQ-EVAP, EQ-BPE). All three are assumption placeholders in the energy balance.

question: What are the spray-dryer inlet, outlet and ambient gas temperatures?
why_it_matters: They set the dryer heater duty, which is the plant utility load (UT-DRYGAS is inlet gas heating from ambient) and the largest thermal load in the train; the outlet also caps the product temperature.
notes: Feeds P-DRY-T-IN, P-DRY-T-OUT and P-DRY-T-AMBIENT. The drying-gas MASS is no longer assumed: it is derived from the process duty, so the earlier gas-to-water ratio parameter has been removed (it had been set to whatever made a test pass). Outlet must stay below the duplex Tm (Q-030) and the powder below its moisture-shifted Tg (Q-039); the particle stays near the wet-bulb temperature while wet (spray-drying finding). All three are temperatures, so none of them resolves annual demand (Q-002).

question: What is the health-based exposure limit (HBEL/PDE) for cleaning validation of the shared filtration and drying equipment?
why_it_matters: Sets the cleaning-validation acceptance limits (MACO, per-swab and per-rinse) for the hard-to-clean evaporator and dryer; no HBEL exists anywhere in the registers.
notes: BLOCKED on data, not on annual demand: a PDE/HBEL cannot be derived without toxicology data that does not exist in the public record for this molecule. The derivation METHOD (PDE then MACO) is a named technology-transfer deliverable (SRC-WHO-TRS1044). Ties R-008 (hard-to-clean CIP/SIP) and R-015. See P-HBEL-DS and the microbial page.

question: Should EQ-UFYIELD use the concentration factor or the volumetric concentration factor, and how are the yield and the retentate volume solved together?
why_it_matters: The membrane-passage loss is exponential in ln(VCF), so which VCF is meant changes the computed UF/DF yield; the two differ by 1/(Y_lig x Y_UFDF) once product loss is accounted for.
notes: The balance computes VCF as P-CONC-UF/P-CONC-LIG (a concentration ratio) while the stream volumes imply a larger volumetric ratio, because the retentate is sized on the API that SURVIVES the step. They coincide only at 100% recovery. Solving them consistently is a fixed point (yield depends on VCF, VCF depends on retentate volume, retentate volume depends on yield), deliberately not attempted here. Documented on the equations page rather than left implicit. See EQ-UFYIELD, P-UFDF-RETENTION, Q-036.

question: What are the minimum working volumes and turndown ratios of the specified vessels, skids and CIP loops?
why_it_matters: Turndown decides whether a small campaign can run at all; it is set by vessel and impeller geometry, minimum crossflow velocity and minimum pump flow - NOT by annual demand, so it must not be parked behind Q-002.
notes: Several equipment turndown entries previously cited Q-002 (annual demand), which is a question that by design is never resolved here, so those gaps were structurally unclosable. Turndown is a dimensionless ratio of a vessel to itself: it is answered by vendor minimum working volumes and loop hydraulics once equipment is selected. The evaporator is the exception already answered in kind, by the minimum wetting rate (P-EVAP-MIN-WETRATE, R-013). See equipment.csv.

question: Which ligase, and in which form: purified/soluble, cell-free extract, or immobilised on a carrier?
why_it_matters: It decides the clearance strategy (denature-then-filter vs retention on the carrier, Q-032), the protein and endotoxin load entering purification (R-017), the ATP optimum (Q-040), the reaction temperature and hold time, and whether an 85 C denature hold - above any plausible duplex Tm - enters the train at all (R-021).
notes: OPEN, with two documented candidates and no basis to choose between them. (1) The T4-mutant CC31 lineage: wild-type T4 DNA ligase 'is poor at ligating 2'-OMe substituted oligonucleotide segments', while wild-type CC31 and its mutants 'are able to ligate a 2' OMe substituted 5' segment' and gave 'substantially greater product+template peak area' (SRC-USPTO-10640812). That patent DOES report conversion - it defines it verbatim as 'product area/(template + product area) * 100', tabulates it, and its Example 13 Table 22 is a nine-point time series - so the blanket negative this note previously carried is struck (corrected 2026-09-25). What is true is narrower and still limits what the patent can settle: Table 22 is normalised to a tri-template hub peak and is therefore a species DISTRIBUTION, not commensurable with that patent's own conversion table nor with the 92 percent carried here from SRC-CN119265174, so the figures must not be pooled; and its best-converting example runs on an all-phosphodiester backbone, while its phosphorothioate/MOE gapmer figures are 11.8 percent or less. It also drags Q-040 with it: wild-type T4 'gave exclusively AppDNA on RNA-splinted substrate' (SRC-PBCV1-2014), and for an siRNA the splint IS the complementary product strand, so the adenylylated dead end (R-010) is a standing hazard for this lineage. (2) PBCV-1 / Chlorella virus DNA ligase: characterised on DNA-RNA HYBRID helices with unmodified DNA donors (SRC-PBCV1-2014), not on a fully modified siRNA duplex - the mechanism transfers, the numbers do not. (3) The one demonstrated fully modified siRNA route uses an RNA ligase / PNK CELL-FREE EXTRACT at 1 mg/mL (SRC-ALMAC-2023, SI), which is a whole proteome plus endotoxin rather than one ligase (R-017); and the one demonstrated immobilised route is IMAC-type non-covalent immobilisation (SRC-CN119265174), the format most prone to leaching. Blocks P-LIG-ENZ-LOAD, P-ENZ-CLEARANCE-LRV, P-LIG-TIME and the two enzyme-clearance rows in the control matrix. (4) THE SOLUBLE BRANCH IMPLIES EQUIPMENT THAT DOES NOT EXIST: an 85 C/15 min denature hold needs a heated vessel or exchanger, and the only candidate item in the register - U02-CF - is single-use depth media and cannot denature anything. That unit is deliberately NOT added to data/equipment.csv, because adding it would half-commit to a branch nobody has chosen; its absence is registered HERE instead, and the product-integrity risk it would create is R-021. Control rows C-011 (soluble) and C-012 (immobilised) carry the fork, both with blank acceptance.

question: Can an in-line variable-pathlength A260 reading actually be qualified on this stream - what is FlowVPX's minimum achievable pathlength, and does any oligonucleotide A260 data exist for it?
why_it_matters: It decides whether C-013 can ever become a closed loop. Three things are missing from the public record and each one alone blocks it.
notes: Registered because the record is genuinely empty, not because nobody has looked. (1) FlowVPX's spec DOC0206 gives a MAXIMUM pathlength of 5.000 mm and a minimum pathlength STEP of 0.001 mm, and never a minimum achievable pathlength - the two are not the same thing (SRC-REPLIGEN-FLOWVPX). Put this to the vendor in writing, because at P-CONC-UF we need less than P-VPE-PATHLENGTH-MIN. (2) No public FlowVPE or FlowVPX dataset exists for ANY oligonucleotide at A260 - every readable dataset is mAb or ADC at A280. (3) No peer-reviewed in-line concentration measurement on an oligonucleotide stream exists by ANY technique. Also note variable-pathlength instruments saturate near their own floor and the documented failure mode is UNDERESTIMATION of concentration - a silent, non-conservative bias. A Repligen-Ionis note titled 'Application of In-Line Variable Pathlength Chromatography for High Concentration Oligonucleotide Solutions' appears in search indexes but returned 404 on three URLs; request it from the vendor. See Q-042, C-013, I-024.

question: What is the 260 nm extinction coefficient of OUR duplex, and at what concentration does a given pathlength saturate?
why_it_matters: It sets the pathlength arithmetic that decides whether an in-line concentration reading is possible on any stream in the train, so it gates Q-042 and C-013.
notes: P-EPS-260 carries a BAND (20-25 mL/mg/cm), not a value, because the mass extinction coefficient is SEQUENCE-SPECIFIC and our sequence is not fixed. The band brackets the standard A260 = 1 conversions for nucleic acid (about 40-50 ug/mL at 1 cm) and allows for duplex hypochromicity; it is a bracket for a feasibility calculation, NOT a quantitation basis. A real assay needs the sequence-specific coefficient. See Q-042, Q-051.

question: Does the instrument tag scheme conform to the current edition of ANSI/ISA-5.1?
why_it_matters: Tags are the primary key between the instrument register, the control matrix and any future P&ID, so a non-conventional scheme is expensive to change later and confusing to an engineering contractor.
notes: UNVERIFIED AND DELIBERATELY SO. The current edition is ANSI/ISA-5.1-2024 (retitled) and its identification-system guidance was SPLIT OUT into ISA-TR5.1.02-2024, so a conformance claim needs both documents; neither was retrieved (SRC-ISA-5-1-2024, SRC-ISA-TR5-1-02-2024) and ISA prohibits entering its intellectual property into AI tools, so no clause text or letter table from either may be reproduced here. The letters used in data/instruments.csv are THIS REPOSITORY'S declared scheme (gen/controls.py TAG_FIRST_LETTERS), including the user's-choice assignments M = moisture and Q = discrete sampled quantity. Buy both documents into document control and check the scheme against them before any P&ID is issued. Note also that area and unit prefixes are NOT specified by ISA at all, so the -0306 style unit-and-loop numbering is ours to define and must not be attributed to ISA.

question: Do the generated process flow diagrams conform to ISO 10628-1, and what symbol set should they actually use?
why_it_matters: The PFD symbol set used here is THIS PROJECT'S OWN, and nothing in the public record that this project has read pins it down. An engineering contractor receiving a non-conformant diagram set has to redraw it, and a symbol that looks standard but is not is worse than one that is obviously bespoke.
notes: DELIBERATELY UNVERIFIED, and named so it cannot be mistaken for conformance. Three documents bear on it and none of them settles it here. (1) ISO 10628-1:2014 (SRC-ISO-10628-1) is the standard that specifies what a BFD and a PFD must contain; DEXPI draws its own reference diagrams from it. It is PAYWALLED and NOT retrieved. This is the document to buy into document control and check the generated diagrams against. (2) DEXPI Process 1.0 (SRC-DEXPI-PROCESS-1-0, read in full) is the open-access anchor actually used here, and section 6.2.2 gives the principle the generator follows - a PFD symbol represents the ACTIVITY carried out, not the equipment - but section 6 also states that FURTHER WORK IS NEEDED to define the presentation layer, so DEXPI does not specify a symbol set either. (3) ANSI/ISA-5.1-2024 governs instrument symbols and is unread and un-reproducible (Q-053). What the generator therefore does: a labelled rectangle per unit operation, and instrument bubbles distinguished only by line style, with the legend stating in the drawing that the symbol set is this project's own. A future revision could map each unit operation onto a DEXPI activity class - the taxonomy is in DEXPI Process 1.0 sections 2.9-2.19, and Evaporating, Drying, Filtering and ReactingChemicals all exist there - but that mapping is a judgement nobody has made yet and is NOT asserted in the data.

question: Which final control element does each closed loop manipulate?
why_it_matters: A detailed PFD is expected to show the final control element - the valve, motor, heater or cooler the loop acts through - and this project cannot draw one, because no register records it. Without it a loop says what it measures but not what it moves, which is the half of a control narrative an engineering contractor needs in order to size and specify anything.
notes: REGISTERED RATHER THAN INVENTED. data/controls.csv records the controlled variable (cpp), the parameter it acts on (param_ref) and the instrument that senses it (instrument_ref), but it has no manipulated-variable and no final-element column, and data/equipment.csv is one row per unit operation with no valves, motors or exchangers in it. DEXPI Process 1.0 section 2.8.1 (SRC-DEXPI-PROCESS-1-0, read in full) expects a PFD to indicate the final control element used, and its section 4.3.2 detailed reference PFD draws control valves manipulating material flows. So the gap is real against the anchor standard, not a stylistic choice. WHAT THE GENERATOR DOES INSTEAD: the actuator stub on a closed loop runs from the bubble to the UNIT BOX, which is what the data actually supports - the loop closes on this unit - and the drawing legend says so. Drawing a valve nobody has specified would be an invention, and would also imply a line-item of equipment that is not in the register. Closing this needs a final-element column and the equipment rows to point at, which is a P&ID-level exercise.

question: Why do seven instruments whose tags declare a control function appear in no control register row - is the control register scoped to CQA-critical loops only, or are seven loops unregistered?
why_it_matters: It decides whether the control register is complete as a control strategy or complete only as a CPP-to-CQA argument, and the two are handed over for different purposes. A reader who takes the register as the full control strategy would under-specify the plant by seven loops.
notes: SURFACED BY DRAWING THE PFD, which is the point of drawing it - nine instrument tags carry an output letter C (control) in the declared scheme (gen/controls.py TAG_OUTPUT_LETTERS), and all nine are in_line measurements, so all nine render as closed loops: TIC-0101, PIC-0301, FIC-0303, TIC-0401, PIC-0402, TIC-0501, TIC-0502, FIC-0504, FIC-0505. Only TWO of them (I-007/TIC-0101 via C-004, and I-035/TIC-0502 via C-009) appear in data/controls.csv. The likely answer is benign - controls.csv is a CPP-to-CQA matrix and an evaporator vacuum loop or a drying-gas flow loop may be ordinary process control with no critical quality attribute behind it - but that scoping has never been written down, and until it is, the register's silence is ambiguous. RESOLVE IT BY WRITING THE SCOPE DOWN, or by adding the missing rows. It must NOT be resolved by inventing control rows to make the counts agree, and it must not be resolved by removing the C from a tag: the tag records a real control function. Counts verified by execution 2026-09-25 against the 49-row instrument register.

question: What is the measured full-length purity of a 5'-PHOSPHORYLATED short 2'-OMe/2'-F/PS block, the material S01/S02 actually receive?
why_it_matters: P-BLOCK-PUR is the exponent base of the drug-substance full-length ceiling (EQ-PURITY), and every measurement behind it is a different material: MOE/DNA gapmer blocks carrying a 5'-DMTr group (SRC-WO2020227618, 93.6-95.6% chromatography-free at 145.5-258 g) or a 6-mer 2'-OMe PS at 81% (SRC-KELLY-OPRD-2025). Neither is a 5'-phosphate block. The ceiling therefore rests on a transferred number and the transfer is not justified by any source.
notes: Raised when the previous point value of 92 was found to be a YIELD misread as a purity ('92.4% yield, 93.6% purity' in the same tuple). Correcting that fixed the arithmetic but not the transfer: the honest statement is that nobody has published this number for our chemistry. Searched and not found. Do not close by widening the band to cover 81% - that mixes two chemistries into one range.

question: Does per-block full-length purity depend on block LENGTH, and does EQ-PURITY's fixed-f model therefore mis-state how the block count trades against purity?
why_it_matters: EQ-PURITY computes the ceiling as f^k with f held constant while k varies. But f is itself a function of block length: under EQ-SPOS a per-cycle yield y gives f = y^(L-1), and splitting a strand into more blocks makes each block SHORTER and so individually purer. Whether the ceiling rises or falls with k depends on whether the junction purity g exceeds y - it falls when g < y, which is the case at any realistic ligation purity, so the register's stated direction holds. But the model does not say that it freezes f, and the trade it describes is therefore stated more confidently than its own arithmetic supports.
notes: P-BLOCK-PUR is measured on 4-5 nt blocks and applied to blocks of unstated length; a 21-mer in 3 blocks needs 7-mers. Resolving this needs a per-cycle yield for OUR chemistry and a junction purity, neither of which is registered. NOT a defect in the note's direction - that was checked and holds - but a gap in what the model admits about itself. See P-N-BLOCKS, EQ-PURITY, EQ-SPOS.

question: What terminates the ligation reaction, at what condition, and does the duplex survive it?
why_it_matters: NO UNIT OPERATION, STREAM OR PARAMETER IMPLEMENTS A QUENCH, which is the gap; the terms themselves are now discussed across the risk, control, coupling and buffer registers. (This row carried a stronger census claim until 2026-09-27 - that quench, inactivat, EDTA, chelat and proteinase returned ZERO hits in every non-sources CSV. Re-measured, that is false: EDTA alone appears in buffers, controls, couplings, risks and this register. It was true when the question was raised and was falsified by the rows the question itself spawned, including its own notes. Corrected rather than deleted, because a census claim that rots is worth seeing.) Every documented PROCESS inactivation sits above the duplex melting band (P-DS-TM 58.1-64.1 C) - 80 C/5 min and 85 C/15 min in SRC-CN119265174, 95 C/5 and 95 C/10 min in SRC-USPTO-10640812, 95 C/20 min in SRC-WO2025262452 - while several batch examples in the SAME patent (SRC-CN119265174 Examples 3, 5, 6 and 8) remove an immobilised enzyme centrifugally with NO thermal hold at all. So the step may be necessary or may not exist, and nothing registered decides which.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25 from the quench beat and verified by re-reading the documents. THE EVIDENCE IS INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY WITHIN ONE DOCUMENT, and that is the finding: SRC-CN119265174 Example 7 heat-kills an IMMOBILISED enzyme at 80 C/5 min, Example 12 heat-kills both an immobilised and a soluble arm at 85 C/15 min, and Examples 3, 5, 6 and 8 take the immobilised enzyme out by centrifugation (3000 rpm, 2 min) with no thermal step. So the thermal hold is not decided by soluble-vs-immobilised (the register's framing, refuted) and it is not decided by batch-vs-flow either (Example 8 is immobilised AND batch AND unheated). A 45 C low endpoint circulated during research and is NOT carried: it traces to a document that could not be retrieved, and the two figures behind it are midpoints of residual-activity curves after a 60 min hold, not melting temperatures - they must never be compared with P-DS-TM as like-for-like. Almac's 75 C/10-30 min is a DIFFERENT quantity again: it is the polynucleotide-kinase kill, applied to single strands before annealing, at 0.5 mM in 96-well plates (SRC-ALMAC-2023) - and it is followed in the same sentence by a centrifugal solids rejection whose supernatant is carried into the ligation, which is a separate gap registered as Q-072. The mitigation the sources point at but nobody has demonstrated here is to CHELATE FIRST and heat only if you must - EDTA stops the reaction, strips the cofactor so the enzyme cannot resume on cooling, and removes the hydrolysis catalyst. See P-LIG-INACT-T, R-021, R-022, C-014. | CORRECTED 2026-09-27 BY RE-RETRIEVING THE DOCUMENTS, and the correction is that A CHEMICAL STOP IS IN THE RETRIEVED RECORD after all - three documents, not the zero this register implied, each quote checked character by character this session. (1) SRC-PBCV1-2014 is the strongest and the only one on a LIGATION, VERBATIM: 'A control reaction was prepared by addition of 25 ul of a stop solution containing 50 mM EDTA and 10 mM Tris-HCl at pH 7.5 before ligase addition. The ligation reactions were then incubated at 37 C with reactions halted at 15, 30, 60, 120, 240 and 480 min by addition of 25 ul stop solution.' Six timepoints, chemically halted, no thermal step - but 2.5 nM unmodified DNA probes on an mRNA splint, an analytical titration and not a process. (2) SRC-NEB-WO2023173098, VERBATIM: 'After quenching with 10 uL of 2x Quench Solution (20 mM EDTA, 2% SDS)', and a second recipe 'quenched by adding 2 ul of 30 mM EDTA and heating at 75 C for 5 min' - EDTA AND heat, which is the shape this register's own mitigation argues for. SCOPE CAVEAT: every quench in that patent is on a capping or poly(A) tailing reaction, never on a ligation. (3) SRC-ALMAC-2023 quenches with methanol at its analytical sampling points, VERBATIM 'quenched by addition of 100% v/v methanol (MeOH)' in the PNK screen and 'quenched by addition of 1 volume (vol.) methanol (MeOH)' in the RNAL screen - ONE recipe written in two units on two different screens, not two independent data points on quench strength. A FOURTH CANDIDATE IS REFUTED AND THE REFUTATION MATTERS MORE THAN THE THREE FINDINGS: SRC-WO2025262452 was said to name a chemical stop one sentence past this register's quote. It does not. VERBATIM: 'The reactions were quenched by heating to 95 C for 20 min to inactivate the enzyme. The inactivated reactions were subsequently diluted 400-fold in 10 mM EDTA pH 7.0 and analyzed via HPLC as described below.' That document calls the HEAT KILL the quench and applies the EDTA to the ALREADY-INACTIVATED reaction as HPLC sample preparation, so this register's existing reading of it is right and the correction offered against it was wrong. WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES FOR THIS QUESTION: the claim that nothing retrieved terminates a reaction chemically is withdrawn, and a quench row becomes supportable - but EVERY chemical stop found is at an ANALYTICAL SAMPLING POINT, and not one of them is a process-scale termination of a modified-siRNA ligation. The question therefore stays OPEN and narrows rather than closing: what is missing is a chemical stop demonstrated on OUR chemistry at OUR scale, with the duplex shown to survive it. The agent and its charge remain blank by design (Q-060). | 2026-09-27 (slice 4 phase 4) THE ANALYTICAL QUENCH IS NOW A REGISTERED SOLUTION AND THE PROCESS QUENCH IS STILL NOT. BUF-QUENCH carries the one chemical stop the register can state - SRC-PBCV1-2014's 50 mM EDTA / 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5 stop solution, 1:1 into a 25 ul reaction - explicitly scoped to a WITHDRAWN ALIQUOT feeding qPCR, on 2.5 nM unmodified DNA probes. It is not an answer to this question: no unit operation was added, P-LIG-INACT-T is untouched, and nothing retrieved terminates a fully modified siRNA ligation at process scale. The three SRC-NEB-WO2023173098 recipes are all on capping or poly(A) tailing and the SRC-ALMAC-2023 methanol quench feeds UPLC, so the shape this question asks for - a chemical stop on a ligation at scale, with evidence the duplex survives it - remains unretrieved.

question: Does a residual-ligase limit exist at all, and on what basis would one be set?
why_it_matters: Q-032 asks the MAGNITUDE of enzyme clearance; this asks the prior question, whether there is a number to clear to. Without a limit, the clearance duty behind R-002 cannot be sized at either end, and the log figures the envelope page computes are conditional on a candidate limit rather than on a specification.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25. ICH Q6B s6.2.1(c) verbatim (verified): 'Downstream-derived impurities include, but are not limited to, enzymes, chemical and biochemical processing reagents ..., inorganic salts ..., solvents, carriers, ligands ..., and other leachables.' So ICH's own taxonomy makes a residual ligase - and an immobilised-carrier leachate - a process-related impurity. But the clearance-study licence in s6.2.1(a) is textually bound to CELL-SUBSTRATE-derived impurities ('to demonstrate the removal of cell substrate-derived impurities such as nucleic acids and host cell proteins ... for these impurities'), and s6.2.1(c) carries no equivalent licence. Extending (a) to (c) is OUR inference and must be written as an argument by analogy to be defended, NOT as an ICH permission. SRC-EMA-OLIGO-2024 s4.3.2 licenses purge arguments but its impurity list omits protein entirely ('protein' occurs 0 times in the whole guideline, verified) and the threshold routes it offers (ICH M7, Q3A, Q3C) are small-molecule routes inapplicable to a protein; its only remaining route is verbatim 'be toxicologically qualified', which makes toxicological qualification the only EU-licensed basis. USP <1132>'s often-quoted '<1 to 100 ng/mg' band must NOT be transferred: it is a protein impurity in a PROTEIN product measured by immunoassay, and ours is the inverted case, a 34-75 kDa protein in a ~14 kDa nucleic-acid duplex. See P-ENZ-CLEARANCE-LRV, Q-032, Q-061, R-002.

question: Which assay can measure residual ligase protein in a 15 g/L modified-duplex matrix, and has it ever been run there?
why_it_matters: I-016 is the single instrument the chromatography-free thesis rests on. If no assay works in this matrix then P-ENZ-CLEARANCE-LRV is blank for TWO independent reasons - no limit (Q-060) and no method - and the thesis has nothing to stand on. This is an analytical gap with a different owner from the process gap in Q-032.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25. EVERY DIRECT-INJECTION TOTAL-PROTEIN METHOD IS EXCLUDED, each for a separately sourced reason. A280 is dominated by the product and USP <1132> s3.2.1.3 admits so in writing - verbatim, 'less specific for protein (e.g., nucleic acids will also be measured)'; at 15 g/L with P-EPS-260 at 20-25 mL/mg/cm, A260 in 1 cm is 300-375 AU, so even a tenth of that at 280 nm is beyond any spectrophotometer's linear range. Bradford's RNA colour yield is about 9 percent of BSA's, which at 15 g/L is roughly 1350 mg/L of apparent BSA-equivalent from the product alone - three to five logs above any plausible limit. Ph. Eur. 2.5.33 Method 1 needs 0.2-2 mg/mL of protein, two to four orders above our analyte, and Method 6 excludes our buffer BY NAME (verbatim: 'Primary amines, such as tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane ... react with phthalaldehyde and must be avoided or removed'). BCA's vendor manual requires a different kit for reducing agents and BUF-LIG carries 1 mM DTT. WHAT THAT SURVEY DOES NOT COVER, stated so the question is not read as broader than its evidence: it addresses only direct injection of the neat pool. Routes that enrich or clean up first - size-exclusion or anion-exchange depletion of the product, protein precipitation, amino-acid analysis after hydrolysis, intrinsic fluorescence - were NOT assessed, and are the obvious next place to look. THE CANDIDATE METHOD, RESTATED 2026-09-25 AFTER A CITATION CHECK FAILED. An earlier version of this row named 'USP <1132.1> Method C, targeted LC-MS/MS against spiked stable-isotope-labelled peptides' with a limit of quantitation of 0.4 ng/mL, and said that Method A was structurally unavailable to us. NONE OF THAT IS CARRIED ANY MORE, because none of it is verifiable from the document this register holds: '1132.1', 'Method C' and 'LLOQ' each return ZERO hits in the retrieved copy of USP <1132>, no chapter <1132.1> is registered in sources.csv at all, and the copy read is of 2016 vintage, which could not contain a later chapter. Attributing a method, a method letter and a sensitivity figure to a chapter nobody here has read is the exact defect class this register exists to prevent, and it was introduced by trusting a research note instead of the document. WHAT SURVIVES THE CHECK is weaker and is quotable: USP <1132> does discuss a peptide-based mass-spectrometric route, verbatim - 'a quantitative HPLC-MS/MS method may be developed, based on monitoring peptides that ionize well from digests of the analytical standard protein and the sample.' So the candidate is an APPROACH, not a compendial procedure, and no sensitivity is claimed for it. TWO CONSEQUENCES, ONE OF WHICH CORRECTS THIS ROW'S OWN EARLIER REASONING. First, that sentence requires an analytical standard OF THE IMPURITY PROTEIN, so the mass-spectrometric route is gated on the enzyme-form decision exactly as an immunoassay is - this row previously said the gating applied only to the immunoassay, and that was wrong (Q-050). Second, the barrier the chapter itself names for this route is 'the overwhelming number of product-derived peptides relative to impurity peptides'; our product is a nucleic acid and contributes NO peptides, so that particular barrier is absent here - which is an inference of ours from the chapter's own reasoning, not a finding in it. See I-016, Q-032, Q-060, Q-050.

question: Does ICH Q7 section 18 apply to the ligation reactor, or only to the ligase supplier's plant?
why_it_matters: Section 18 is the only part of ICH Q7 that speaks to a biologically catalysed step at all, so several information requirements in the checklist lean on it. If it does not reach our step, those rows lose their anchor and become inference.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25. ICH Q7 section 18 is headed 'SPECIFIC GUIDANCE FOR APIs MANUFACTURED BY CELL CULTURE/FERMENTATION'. Our active substance is NOT manufactured that way - it is chemically synthesised and then enzymatically joined - but the enzyme REAGENT is a fermentation product, so section 18 may govern the ligase supplier's plant and reach ours only by analogy. TWO CHARACTERISATIONS IN THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS QUESTION WERE WRONG AND ARE WITHDRAWN, both caught by the acceptance panel. s18.41 is NOT a clause about enzyme removal: verbatim it reads 'Harvest and purification procedures that remove or inactivate the producing organism, cellular debris and media components ... should be adequate to ensure that the intermediate or API is recovered with consistent quality' - the subject is the ORGANISM THAT MADE the product, not a catalyst deliberately added to a chemical step. And s18.33 is not about terminating a reaction: it lists critical operating parameters to be monitored, verbatim 'temperature, pH, agitation rates, addition of gases, pressure'. Reading either as an enzyme clause contradicted the decisive negative this question is built on, which I re-verified: 'enzym' and 'biocatal' each return ZERO hits across all 49 pages of Q7 and all 30 of Q11. That is the finding - there is no enzyme clause in either document to be scoped in or out - and inventing one from an adjacent paragraph was the opposite of what this question exists to record. See infoneeds.csv anchor_strength, SRC-ICH-Q7.

question: Is the in-force EMA guideline on the chemistry of active substances applicable to a synthetic oligonucleotide?
why_it_matters: EMA/CHMP/QWP/49484/2026 section 4.2.3 carries the ONLY directly-worded enzyme clause found in any in-force guideline, so whether it reaches this process decides whether the enzyme information requirement is anchored or inferred.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25. The clause is worth having and is verbatim: 'For enzymes used in the process, the origin (recombinant, animal or herbal origin) should be indicated and the possibility of specific impurities from the reaction to the final substance should be discussed.' The same section carries the strongest imperative in it - 'Relevant viral safety and/or TSE data must be provided if any material of animal or human origin is used ... (e.g. arising from fermentation, enzymes, amino acids, etc.)'. BUT THE SCOPE IS UNSTATED IN OUR FAVOUR AND POSSIBLY AGAINST US: section 2 excludes biological and biotechnological products, and the word 'oligonucleotide' appears ZERO times in the guideline. Applicability to a synthetic oligonucleotide joined enzymatically is therefore arguable and is NOT asserted. RETRIEVAL TRAP recorded with it: two published URLs still serve the 2024 DRAFT, and only the live guideline URL serves the CHMP-adopted final text - a citation of the draft is a citation of a superseded document. See SRC-EMA-CHEM-AS-2026, infoneeds.csv.

question: Is there any ligation datapoint between 1.5 mM and 10 mM segment concentration?
why_it_matters: Reactor volume scales inversely with concentration, so this is the single parameter that most directly sizes U01-LIG. The evidence is two clusters with a void between them, and the void is exactly where a plant would want to operate. Its width is itself unknown - between about 2x and about 6x depending on a basis neither document states (see the notes), where this row previously said 6.7x flatly.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25. THE SPAN 1.5-10 mM IS NOT A RANGE AND MUST NOT BE WRITTEN AS ONE: its low end is a SUCCESS point and its high end is a FAILURE point, which is a different kind of claim at each end. Low: 1.5 mM per segment reaching 89.50 percent product at 16 h (SRC-USPTO-10640812 Example 13, Table 22, verified) - but on a PHOSPHODIESTER 2'-MOE gapmer with a NAD-dependent ligase in a 4 mL immobilised packed bed, and the same patent's phosphorothioate/MOE numbers are 11.8 percent or less, so the best-converting concentration is on a backbone we do not have. Its low end also crosses cofactor and buffer (50 mM KH2PO4 pH 7.5, NAD+, no Tris, no DTT, no ATP). High: 10 mM blockmer, where reactions were verbatim 'slow and failed to go completion' (SRC-ALMAC-2023) - qualitative, with no conversion, time, temperature, enzyme or scale. Between them: nothing of any kind. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: a conversion-versus-time curve at 3-6 mM on a fully modified phosphorothioate siRNA duplex, at a stated scale, from a source independent of Almac. Note the mechanism that predicts the void is real even though its number does not transfer - substrate inhibition, fitted over 30 nM-20 uM on a different enzyme - so raising concentration buys volumetric loading and pays it back in rate. See P-LIG-SEG-CONC, P-CONC-LIG, Q-016, Q-066. | THE 6.7x VOID IS BASIS-DEPENDENT AND THE TWO ENDS ARE NOT STATED ON THE SAME BASIS - established 2026-09-27 by re-retrieving both documents. THE LOW END IS PER SEGMENT, AND THE MIX CARRIES A FOURTH OLIGONUCLEOTIDE THIS REGISTER HAS NEVER MENTIONED. SRC-USPTO-10640812 Example 13 lists its 5 mL charge line by line, VERBATIM: '108 ul 0.07011M centre segment (1.5 mM final) / 137 ul 0.05481 M 3'-segment (1.5 mM final) / 168 ul 0.04461 M 5'-segment (1.5 mM final) / 750 ul 0.00387M Hub (Template) (0.55 mM final)'. So it is 1.5 mM of EACH of three segments - 4.5 mM - PLUS 0.55 mM of tri-template hub, and the total oligonucleotide loading is 5.05 mM, not 1.5. THE HUB HAS NO COUNTERPART IN OUR ROUTE, and that is not an assumption: it is, VERBATIM, 'A tri-template hub (approximately 24 kDa) comprising a support material referred to as the hub and three template sequences... Each copy of the template was covalently attached, at its own individual attachment point, to the hub', and it exists so that it 'is a higher molecular weight than the target (product) oligonucleotide... thereby allowing it to be retained when the impurities and products are separated'. SRC-ALMAC-2023 needs no such species at all - the word 'template' occurs EXACTLY ONCE in its whole main text and it is the product's own overhang, VERBATIM: 'The overhang serves as a template for the next annealing step in the alternate strand.' So 0.55 mM of the low end's loading is a supported reagent our route does not have. THE HIGH END'S BASIS IS SIMPLY NOT STATED: 'starting blockmer concentrations as high as 10 mM' does not say whether 10 mM is each blockmer or the sum, and the same paper says each ligation step starts with THREE blockmers. WHAT THAT DOES TO THE WIDTH, arithmetic ours: on a total-oligonucleotide basis the void is 10/5.05 = 2.0x if Almac's 10 mM is a total, 4.0x if it is per blockmer over two, and 5.9x over three. The 6.7x figure is 10/1.5 - it is the width only in the case where the high end is per blockmer AND the hub is excluded, and it was published as though it were the width unconditionally. THE HONEST STATEMENT IS THAT THE VOID IS BETWEEN ABOUT 2x AND ABOUT 6x WIDE AND THE DOCUMENTS DO NOT SAY WHICH. None of this narrows the void or makes the endpoints comparable - it makes the interval's own width unknown on top of its two ends being different kinds of claim, so the refusal to write a range is if anything better founded than before. See Q-064, Q-071.

question: Is there a jacket heating duty and a heating utility for the 65 C anneal, and does the anneal stay in U01-LIG at scale?
why_it_matters: The anneal is a real, sourced, non-optional step (65 C for 15 min before every ligation) and NO utility in the register heats a reactor jacket: UT-STEAM is evaporator duty plus SIP and UT-CHILL is cooling. So a documented duty has no utility behind it, and at scale it may not fit the vessel at all.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25, and it is a gap in a DUTY and a UTILITY, not a missing unit - U01-LIG already exists and is the right vessel, so nothing here bears on Q-050 or on the denature-unit question. The anneal condition is verified verbatim: blockmers annealed 'for 15 min at 65 C', then 'cooled to RT before being kept on ice' (SRC-ALMAC-2023, P-LIG-ANNEAL-T, P-LIG-ANNEAL-HOLD). THE SCALE ARGUMENT, ours and first-principles: for geometrically similar vessels the specific heat-transfer area falls as the cube root of volume, so 1 L to 1000 L loses exactly 10x in area per unit volume and a 15 min ramp becomes of order 150 min at the same jacket temperature difference - or the anneal must leave the reactor for a higher-area device. That is an unregistered equipment fork and it sizes both the jacket and the temperature-control unit. The ceiling on jacket temperature on the way DOWN is set by enzyme stability rather than by the duplex, and the enzyme figure is not registered because the document behind it could not be retrieved (Q-059). Reaction enthalpy is negligible against the ramp by about three orders of magnitude, so the sensible duty is the whole of it. See UT-HOTW, U01-LIG.

question: What is the substrate-inhibition constant Ki for our ligase on our fully modified blockmers?
why_it_matters: It is the mechanistic form of Q-016 and it decides whether concentrating the ligation can ever shrink the plant. If the inhibition constant sits near process concentration, volumetric loading and reaction rate cancel and a bigger titre buys nothing.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25. The only retrieved Ki is 30-36 uM, from a rate law of the form V0 per unit enzyme = kcat*S / (Km + S*(1 + S/Ki)), with S the substrate concentration fitted over 30 nM to 20 uM on 12-bp modified RNA fragments - so the constant sits JUST ABOVE the top of its own fitted range and is an extrapolation, on a different enzyme from any candidate here. The MECHANISM transfers and the NUMBER does not, which is the whole point of registering this separately: substrate inhibition predicts qualitatively what SRC-ALMAC-2023 observed at 10 mM ('slow and failed to go completion') without supplying a figure for our system. The document behind the rate law could not be retrieved this session, so no kcat, Km or Ki is carried in any register row. See Q-064, Q-016, P-LIG-SEG-CONC.

question: What is the LOQ, the precision and the stopping rule of the ligation-conversion IPC in our matrix?
why_it_matters: C-005 holds the reaction to a conversion endpoint rather than to a clock, so the endpoint decision is only as good as the assay behind it - and the register names no method, no limit of quantitation, no precision and no rule for when conversion has stopped moving.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25, and it SHARPENS C-005 rather than weakening it - I checked whether that control asserted something nobody could execute and the arithmetic says it does not. The demonstrated method runs on OUR exact buffer in 12.5 minutes (SRC-ALMAC-2023, SI Table S3: Acquity Peptide BEH C18 300 A 1.7 um 2.1x50 mm, 95 mM HFIP / 16 mM TEA / 5 uM EDTA, 1 mL/min, 80 C, 5 uL, 260 nm), and the reaction moves only about 0.70 percentage points per hour near its endpoint, so a 30-60 min turnaround costs 0.35-0.70 points against 1.40 points of remaining travel. The gate is answerable. WHAT IS MISSING IS THE METROLOGY: no LOQ, no relative standard deviation and no replicate count is published for a ligation-conversion IPC in any matrix, and the only noise indicator available is the non-monotonic 0.1-0.3 point scatter in the segment columns of one table, which is combined assay-plus-process variation and not a precision figure. The three LOQ endpoints that exist for oligonucleotide impurity work - 0.1 percent relative to parent, an approximately 0.2 percent community reporting threshold, 0.3 percent by 2D-LC - are every one of them a purified SINGLE STRAND at about 50 ug/mL on column in clean mobile phase. Not one is a duplex and not one is in Tris/KCl/MgCl2/DTT at 15 g/L, so none is carried as a range here. TWO CONSEQUENCES. At 15 g/L an undiluted 5 uL injection is about 75 ug and grossly overloads the column, so a 10-50x dilution is mandatory - harmless for a relative-area measurement, and the reason this assay can never also see an absolute trace like residual protein (Q-061). And the demonstrated method's oven runs at 80 C, above the duplex melting band (P-DS-TM 58.1-64.1 C), so it is a DENATURING separation and a single conversion number answers the denaturing question only - which is Q-044 biting at the ligation step, not merely at drug substance. See C-005, P-LIG-CONV, Q-010.

question: Are this project's process parameters expressible in scale-independent form, as ICH Q8(R2) s2.4.4 expects?
why_it_matters: Almost every parameter in the register is scale-DEPENDENT - a volume, a concentration in a named vessel, an agitation rate - so a range demonstrated at one scale carries no guarantee at another. That is the defect this repository keeps finding in its own rows, and ICH names the remedy explicitly.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25. ICH Q8(R2) s2.4.4 is direct and quotable: 'if a product was determined to be shear sensitive in a mixing operation, the design space could include shear rate, rather than agitation rate. Dimensionless numbers and/or models for scaling can be included.' Measured against that, this register does badly and the examples are concrete. P-CONC-LIG is a concentration whose whole meaning depends on the vessel it was measured in. P-LIG-ANNEAL-HOLD is a 15 minute ramp that becomes of order 150 minutes at 1000 L purely from the cube-root area law, so the number is scale-bound while looking absolute (CPL-006). The U01-LIG turndown was justified for a whole slice by a shear claim with the sign backwards, which is precisely the error a dimensionless specific-power group would have made visible. AND THE ONE PLACE A SCALE-INDEPENDENT FORM IS AVAILABLE, IT IS ALREADY USED: the evaporator's turndown is set by a minimum wetting rate in kg per metre per second (P-EVAP-MIN-WETRATE, R-013), which is exactly the kind of quantity s2.4.4 asks for - so this is a gap in coverage, not in capability. What would close it is a per-parameter pass deciding which have a dimensionless or intensive equivalent, and saying so where they do not.

question: Which utility generates the evaporator vacuum, and what is its duty?
why_it_matters: P-EVAP-T-BOIL is explicitly a VACUUM boiling window of 40-60 C and an instrument measures the vacuum boiling temperature, but no vacuum-generation utility exists in the register - the utilities are water, clean steam, drying gas, chilled water, compressed air/nitrogen and now jacket heating. A duty with no utility behind it cannot be costed, sized or connected.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25 BY THE ACCEPTANCE PANEL, and it is the same defect class as the one UT-HOTW was registered to close, one unit operation over - which is the useful part. The exhaustive listing of utilities done for the 65 C anneal established that nothing heats a reactor jacket; it did not ask the same question of the evaporator, and the gap was sitting next to it. Not closed here: sizing a vacuum system needs the evaporator's leak load, condenser duty and non-condensable load, none of which is registered, and the evaporator type is itself unselected (Q-018, Q-045). Registered rather than filled, and deliberately NOT given a utility row, because a row with no duty behind it would be the mirror of the defect it is meant to fix. See P-EVAP-T-BOIL, U04-EVAP, UT-CHILL, ENV-013.

question: The EU oligonucleotide guideline is still a draft. What is binding in the meantime, and will the final text reach an enzymatic route?
why_it_matters: It is the ONLY oligonucleotide-specific guideline of any status, and several information requirements in the checklist have no other anchor. A draft anchors nothing: consultation closed 31 January 2025 and it has not been finalised, so a requirement taken from it is an expectation of where the rules are heading, not a rule.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-25 BY THE ACCEPTANCE PANEL, against this project's own text. Eight rows of infoneeds.csv described SRC-EMA-OLIGO-2024 as 'the one in-force oligonucleotide guideline' while that source's own register entry reads 'STILL A DRAFT. Consultation closed 31/01/2025 and it has not been finalised' and its citation field literally begins 'EMA draft Guideline'. The claim was false against evidence already in the register, and presenting a draft as binding is the exact failure mode the anchor_strength column was added to prevent - so the checklist committed it in the same slice that introduced the guard against it. All eight rows are corrected. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN, and it is two things. First, what binds today: the in-force general guideline on the chemistry of active substances (SRC-EMA-CHEM-AS-2026) contains the word 'oligonucleotide' zero times and excludes biological and biotechnological products, so it may not reach this product either (Q-063) - which would leave no oligonucleotide-specific instrument in force at all. Second, whether the final text changes the one sentence that matters here: the draft declines enzymatic synthesis as 'too premature to be included', and a final text that keeps that sentence leaves the route unaddressed while a final text that drops it could create requirements this register has not anticipated. Neither is knowable now. Re-check the EMA status page before relying on any clause taken from it.

question: Almac's main text says the telescoped phosphorylation ran at 5 mM and its own SI says 2 mM for the same experiment - which is it?
why_it_matters: It sets the dilution the phosphorylation-to-ligation handoff imposes, and therefore a vessel fill requirement rather than a bookkeeping detail: both documents agree the ligation runs at 1 mM, so 2 mM means V to 2V in one vessel and 5 mM means V to 5V. The two readings size U01-LIG differently by a factor of 2.5, and the larger one also worsens the 65 C anneal jacket problem (Q-065) by arriving at the top fill.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-27, and it is a contradiction IN THE PUBLISHED RECORD rather than a gap in ours - which is why it is registered as a question and neither number is carried anywhere. BOTH DOCUMENTS WERE RETRIEVED THIS SESSION AND BOTH QUOTES CHECKED CHARACTER BY CHARACTER, with two independent PDF text extractors (pdfminer.six and pypdf) agreeing on every one. MAIN TEXT, VERBATIM: 'Reaction parameter investigation allowed for final phosphorylation at 5 mM blockmer concentration, with a one-pot phosphorylation of 1.2 and 1.3 (5'OH) with PNK-101. The reaction product was successfully telescoped into a ligation reaction with 1.4 to form the antisense strand followed by addition and ligation of 1.1 to yield the full-length duplex (Figure S5).' SI, VERBATIM: 'Phosphorylation of the 5'-OH blockmers at 2 mM concentration was telescoped into the ligation reaction at 1 mM concentration by sequential ligation of 1.4 to form the antisense strand and following ligation of 1.1 to yield the full-length duplex as shown in Figure S5.' IT IS THE SAME EXPERIMENT BY EVERY IDENTIFIER EITHER DOCUMENT GIVES: same one-pot phosphorylation of 1.2 and 1.3, same sequential ligation of 1.4 then 1.1, same Figure S5. TOKEN COUNTS, MEASURED NOT ASSERTED: standalone '5 mM' occurs exactly ONCE in the main text and NEVER in the SI; '2 mM' occurs three times in the SI and never in the main text, and all three SI occurrences are the ATP row of Tables S1 and S2 rather than the telescoping sentence, which spells 2 mM inline. So the two figures never co-occur and nothing in either document reconciles them - there is no erratum, no footnote and no 'corrected to'. WHY IT IS NOT SAFE TO PREFER EITHER: the SI is normally the more detailed record and would usually win, but the main text is the peer-reviewed, typeset artefact and its sentence is the more specific of the two ('Reaction parameter investigation allowed for final phosphorylation at...'), reading as the outcome of an optimisation. A reader who picks one is guessing. THIS IS NOT THE CONTRADICTION IN Q-059: that one is inside SRC-CN119265174 and is about ENZYME INACTIVATION (80 C/5 min vs 85 C/15 min vs centrifugal removal with no thermal step). This one is inside SRC-ALMAC-2023 and is about the PHOSPHORYLATION CHARGE CONCENTRATION. Two documents, two different defects; conflating them would make the register read as though one paper had both. RETRIEVAL HAZARD FOR ANY RE-CHECK: the main text writes 5'OH with a PRIME (U+2032) and no hyphen, the SI writes 5'-OH with a RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK (U+2019) and a hyphen, so a quote transcribed with the wrong character will not string-match either document. See P-LIG-SEG-CONC, P-CONC-LIG, Q-016, Q-064, Q-072.

question: Does the phosphorylation-to-ligation handoff need a solids-rejection step, and what is the precipitate?
why_it_matters: The only retrieved description of that handoff centrifuges the heat-treated reaction and carries the SUPERNATANT into the ligation, so a phase separation sits on the product path where the flowsheet has none. If the solid is denatured cell-free-extract protein the step is an enzyme-removal duty that bears on the ligase-clearance case; if it is precipitated oligonucleotide it is an unquantified yield loss. Nothing retrieved decides which, and the two readings size different equipment.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-27 from a re-read of SRC-ALMAC-2023's methods, and the unregistered part is the SOLIDS REJECTION rather than the thermal hold - Q-059 already records the 75 C hold as the polynucleotide-kinase kill. VERBATIM, the whole sentence: 'Prior to reactions being used for ligations, the samples were heat treated at 75 C for 10 min (initial reactions) or 30 min (crude reactions), then centrifuged to pellet any precipitated material and supernatant used for ligations.' THREE CENTRIFUGATIONS APPEAR IN THAT PAPER AND ONLY THIS ONE IS A PROCESS STEP: the other two follow a methanol quench and feed UPLC vials, whereas this one's supernatant is stated to be what goes into the ligation. That is a phase separation on the product path, and NO unit operation in equipment.csv removes solids between phosphorylation and ligation. TWO CONDITIONS, NOT A RANGE: 10 min and 30 min are keyed to reaction type (initial vs crude) and must not be written as '10-30 min', which is how docs/sources/ligation-evidence.md previously had it. SCALE CAVEAT, and it is the reason this is a question rather than a row: the sentence sits inside the 'PNK Screening Reaction' methods paragraph, whose stated format is 96 well plates at 0.5 mM blockmer, so nothing here demonstrates the step at the 1 L scale the same paper reports for ligation - and a plate centrifuge is not evidence for a disc stack or a filter. WHAT THE PRECIPITATE IS, IS ALSO UNKNOWN: the paper says only 'any precipitated material'. Denatured cell-free-extract protein is the obvious candidate after a 75 C hold, in which case the step is an enzyme-removal duty and couples to Q-050 and Q-032; if it is precipitated oligonucleotide it is a yield loss nobody has quantified. Nothing retrieved decides which, and the two readings size different equipment. NOT CONFLATED WITH THE EXISTING CENTRIFUGATION EVIDENCE: every centrifug* mention already in data/ (C-014, ENV-005, U02-CF, IMP-LIGASE, IN-017, P-LIG-INACT-T, Q-059) is about SRC-CN119265174 removing an IMMOBILISED enzyme at 3000 rpm for 2 min, a different duty on a different material at a different point in the route. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE HERE: no unit operation was added. pfd.UNITS is derived from equipment.csv so a PFD cannot be opted out of, and a new product stream would force a flowsheet width fix and an SVG re-baseline - all of which would land a drawing change on the strength of a 96-well-plate observation. See Q-059, Q-060, Q-050, Q-032, P-LIG-INACT-T.

question: Which of the nine remaining 89-96 percent block-purity citations mean the retracted measured band and which mean the first-principles band?
why_it_matters: Q-011 retracted 89-96 percent as a measurement and P-BLOCK-PUR now carries 93.6-95.6, but nine sites still quote the old band, six of them calling it measured. Cubed over three blocks the two bands give 70-88 versus 82-87 percent, so the drug-substance purity ceiling this repo publishes depends on which one a reader lands on.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-27, and it was found by a GUARD rather than by reading: correcting _QUANTITY in test_numeric_claims_in_prose_carry_a_citation so that it finally matches a percentage surfaced one prose line cubing a block purity the register no longer holds. Q-011 retracted 89-96 percent as the measured chromatography-free band on 2026-09-25 - its low end was an 89.1 percent purity measured at 6.00 g, a bench datum presented inside a band advertised as 145-258 g - and P-BLOCK-PUR and ENV-001 were corrected to 93.6-95.6 percent. THE RETRACTION DID NOT REACH THE PROSE. Measured by sweep, six hand-written sites still present 89-96 percent as a measurement: docs/process/blocks.md:9, docs/findings/filtration.md:92 and :103, docs/equations/index.md:21 and :29, and docs/sources/reading-list.md:466. Three CSV notes do the same - controls.csv C-001, and the SRC-WO2020227618 and SRC-KELLY-OPRD-2025 rows of sources.csv. docs/findings/filtration.md:156 was the seventh and IS fixed, because the corrected guard refused to let it pass. WHAT MAKES THIS SUBTLER THAN A STALE NUMBER: 89-96 percent has a SECOND and still-valid life as the FIRST-PRINCIPLES band, 0.97^4 to 0.99^4 from the 1-3 percent per-cycle failure rate in SRC-US6087491, which ENV-002 carries as an independent reproduction. So the band is not simply wrong - it is a computed band being cited as a measured one, and an edit that deletes it everywhere would destroy a real corroboration. Each of the nine sites has to be read to decide which of the two it meant. The arithmetic consequence is material and not cosmetic: cubed for three blocks, 89-96 gives 70-88 percent where 93.6-95.6 gives 82-87, so the retracted band understates the internal-limited purity floor by about twelve points at its low end and the drug-substance ceiling moves with it. NOT FIXED IN THIS PHASE, deliberately: it is nine judgement calls across six pages and three registers, none of them forced by the phase this was found in, and a silent bulk edit is how the first band got out of step in the first place. See Q-011, Q-057, P-BLOCK-PUR, ENV-001, ENV-002.

question: What caustic strength, temperature and contact time remove OUR soil, and from what measurement?
why_it_matters: Every unit operation in the train is cleaned with the same caustic and nothing has ever cleaned this soil - a ligated fully modified duplex plus RNA-ligase/PNK extract protein in Tris/KCl/MgCl2/DTT, dried onto stainless and onto a TFF membrane. The recipe sets the CIP water and caustic demand the balance does not yet carry, the rinse volume, and whether one chemistry can serve both the vessels and the cassettes. BUF-CIP carries an estimate against this question and does not close it.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-27 by slice 4 phase 4, as the question BUF-CIP's estimate leaves open. WHAT THE RECORD HAS, AND IT IS NOT A SPECIFICATION FOR US. (1) A MEASUREMENT ON THE WRONG SOIL: SRC-ATWELL-2017 ran 90 full-factorial coupon cleans on brewery soil at ambient and found 'NaOH needs to be at least 1% w/v for the clean to be effective' with 'no additional cleaning benefit' above 1% w/v. That is a real threshold-and-saturation curve, on a yeast/protein food soil, on stainless, cold. (2) TWO VENDOR BRACKETS FOR MEMBRANES, which are one convention rather than two measurements - see Q-075. (3) A BOOKKEEPING PLACEHOLDER: SRC-ISPE-WIENCEK-2006 'Assume a nominal chemical concentration of 1% by volume for caustic and acid washes', used only to turn 720,000 L of water into 7,200 L of chemical in a waste-savings sum. It agrees with (1) to one significant figure and that agreement is a COINCIDENCE, not corroboration. WHAT WOULD ANSWER IT is named by the same ISPE article: 'Cleanability studies utilizing soiled coupon testing may identify the proper cleaning chemistry and temperature at a bench top scale.' A coupon study on the real soil, on both materials of construction, closes this question and nothing short of it does. NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS Q-047: that asks what residue limit the cleaning must reach (an HBEL/PDE, a division), this asks what chemistry reaches it. A limit with no recipe and a recipe with no limit are different gaps and both are open. TEMPERATURE IS THE WEAKEST LEG: SRC-ATWELL-2017 cleaned at ambient, SRC-CYTIVA-HF says 20 C 'is not recommended' and prefers 50 C while refusing above 60 C, and SRC-CYTIVA-CFF's own table prescribes 20 C for a hypochlorite/caustic blend. Our soil differs from all of theirs in the one way that matters most for a hot caustic wash: it carries a protein (the ligase) AND a polyanion that is NOT degraded by caustic (SRC-EGLI-2023, and see BUF-CIP).

question: Is the recurring 0.1-0.5 N caustic membrane-cleaning bracket a measurement or an inherited convention, and which vendor's temperature rule governs?
why_it_matters: BUF-MEMBRANE-CLEAN is published as a fact because it is printed in a vendor document, and a reader is entitled to know that the same four numbers recur across vendors, product lines, polymers AND unit operations without changing - which is the signature of copied legacy text, not of two independent measurements. It decides whether the bracket may be treated as a design space for the UF/DF cleaning step or only as what two vendors happen to print, and it decides which temperature end is safe.
notes: RAISED 2026-09-27 by slice 4 phase 4, with the evidence for the convention reading already gathered and re-retrieved. FOUR THINGS POINT THE SAME WAY. (1) THE NUMBERS SURVIVE A UNIT CHANGE: SRC-MILLIPORE-PELLICON3 prints '0.1 N - 0.5 N ... 25 - 50 C ... 30 - 60 min' for cleaning; SRC-CYTIVA-CFF prints '0.1 to 0.5 M NaOH (pH 13) for 30 to 60 minutes at 30 C to 50 C' for SANITIZATION AND DEPYROGENATION. Same numbers, N versus M, different unit operation. (2) THEY SURVIVE A MEMBRANE CHANGE: the Millipore sanitization, depyrogenation and storage tables each give ONE caustic row covering 'Ultracel / Biomax', two membranes the same document otherwise treats as chemically different (peracetic acid and benzyl alcohol for one, hypochlorite and an acetic/phosphoric blend for the other). (3) THEY DO NOT SURVIVE CONTACT WITH A THIRD DOCUMENT: SRC-CYTIVA-HF, on polysulfone hollow fibre, circulates a POINT - '0.5N NaOH at 50 C' for 1 hour - and reproduces neither the 0.1 N end nor the 30-60 min span. So the claim that an identical bracket recurs across two vendors is true of Millipore and the Cytiva CFF handbook and FALSE of the Cytiva hollow-fibre handbook. (4) THE PRINTED pH IS WRONG IN ONE OF THEM: 'pH 10 - 11' beside 0.1-0.5 N NaOH is arithmetically impossible (pH 13.0-13.7), Cytiva prints pH 13 for the same solution, and SRC-ATWELL-2017 MEASURED 'NaOH solutions will have a pH of approximately 13'. The Millipore figure is the hypochlorite row's pH standing beside a caustic row, so it is not carried anywhere in this repository. TWO THINGS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE BRACKET WHEREVER IT GOES: Millipore caps CUMULATIVE exposure - 'Total exposure time must not exceed 100 hours' - with no counterpart in any Cytiva document, so merging the sources silently discards the budget; and Millipore discourages its own top end - 'There is an initial NWP decline in Pellicon 3 Cassettes after initial exposure to 0.5N NaOH. Better membrane life has been observed at lower concentrations.'
